components.name: Top bar
components.description: The primary navigation and branding header at the top of a screen. Supports merchant branding in large, medium, and small configurations, plus minimal states for deep-flow screens.

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: Controls height and merchant branding area

properties.name: Title bar
properties.notes: Shows a secondary title bar row beneath the main bar

properties.name: show Stroke
properties.notes: Bottom border/divider line below the bar

variants.name: Large - Merch
variants.semantic_use: Full-height bar with merchant branding — use on home / main landing screens

variants.name: Med - Merch
variants.semantic_use: Medium height with merchant branding — use on mid-level category screens

variants.name: Small - Merch
variants.semantic_use: Compact bar with merchant branding — use on sub-category or list screens

variants.name: Small - No merch
variants.semantic_use: Compact bar without merchant branding — use on transactional or utility screens

variants.name: Minimum
variants.semantic_use: Bare minimum bar (no title bar) — use on payment flows, full-screen modals, and deep utility screens

use_cases.context: Persistent top navigation on any screen
use_cases.config: Choose the size and title bar combination matching screen hierarchy and available vertical space

rules: Always match the Size to the screen's depth in the navigation hierarchy — use Large - Merch on the home screen and step down for deeper screens.
Use show Stroke=True when screen content begins immediately below the bar; set show Stroke=False when content scrolls underneath and the bar is floating or transparent.
Never place a Title bar=True on the Minimum size — that combination does not exist.
Use Minimum only for focused flows (e.g. checkout, payments, deep settings) where merchant branding would distract.
Minimum only exists with Title bar=False.
Small - Merch and Small - No merch only exist with Title bar=True.
Small - No merch has no show Stroke=False variant — the stroke is always visible on that size.

properties.default: This is a title and it can span 2 lines

properties.name: Body text
properties.default: This is body and it spans 1 line

variants.name: Orange
variants.semantic_use: Brand — use for notifications related to POP brand moments, rewards, or brand-specific communications

use_cases.context: Showing a brief non-blocking feedback message after a user action

rules: Never place Toast directly in screens. Always use Toastbar - Organism wherever a toast notification is needed — it handles positioning, dismissal behaviour, and animation correctly.
Match the State to the semantic context — Orange only for brand, Green for success, Red for errors, White for neutral system messages. Never use Green for errors or Red for success.

components.name: Toastbar - Organism
components.description: A sticky, full-width notification bar that persists until dismissed or auto-expires. Used for promotions, system alerts, and time-sensitive nudges anchored to the top or bottom of a screen.

properties.name: Swipe up dismiss

variants.name: None

variants.name: Cross
variants.semantic_use: User can manually dismiss the bar

variants.name: Button
variants.semantic_use: Bar contains an actionable CTA button

use_cases.context: Sticky full-width notification — brief post-action feedback as well as persistent screen-level notifications

rules: Use Toastbar - Organism for all toast notifications — brief post-action feedback (payment confirmed, error, copy) as well as persistent screen-level notifications.
Always set Title text — never leave the placeholder copy in production.
Auto dismiss 3s=True is the default — only disable it when the notification is critical and must remain visible until user action.
Swipe up dismiss=True always stays enabled unless the toast action is mandatory.
Match the Colour to the semantic context — Orange only for brand, Green for success, Red for errors, White for neutral.

components.name: Bottom sheet
components.description: A modal panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen to present a focused set of actions, details, or confirmations. Slot 1 and Slot 2 are dynamic-height slots.

properties.name: Title + Body
properties.notes: Shows the title and body text block

properties.name: Body
properties.notes: Shows body text within the sheet

variants.name: Default
variants.semantic_use: Solid-background sheet — standard confirmations, forms, detail panels

variants.name: Transparent
variants.semantic_use: Transparent background — overlays on media or image-heavy screens

use_cases.context: Presenting a focused set of actions, details, or confirmations in a modal overlay anchored to the bottom

rules: Always set Tap outside dismiss=True unless the action inside the sheet is mandatory and cannot be abandoned.
Type=Transparent is for special visual contexts only — default to Type=Default for all standard flows.
No inside scroll — slot container height is fixed; content that exceeds it will clip. Avoid long lists or dynamic-length stacks that could overflow.
Always place content inside the slot, not directly on the slot container frame — placing on the container breaks the height-hugging behaviour.

components.name: Bottom sheet - Segmented
components.description: A bottom sheet displaying multi-category tabbed content — e.g. payment method categories, filter tabs, account sections. Sheet content and Slot are dynamic-height slots.

properties.name: Sheet content
properties.notes: Content slot for the active tab

use_cases.context: Displaying multi-category tabbed content in a bottom sheet (2–4 categories)

rules: Use Bottom sheet - Segmented only when content has 2–4 distinct categories that benefit from tab navigation. For single-category content, use the standard Bottom sheet.
Do not use DON'T USE - Buttons — it is a legacy slot retained for backward compatibility only. Use the Button variant and CTA - Cat props instead.
No inside scroll — slot container height is fixed; content that exceeds it will clip.
Always place content inside the slot, not directly on the slot container frame.

components.name: Popup

use_cases.context: Presenting a critical prompt requiring user decision — autopay approval, permission request, offer acceptance

rules: Tap outside to dismiss=False is the default — only enable it for non-critical informational popups where abandonment is acceptable.
Always provide at least one CTA — never show a Popup without an actionable button.
Use State=Success only after a successful transaction or setup — never as the initial state.
Expiry highlight=True is for time-sensitive offers only — turn it off for non-expiring content.
Keep Title text concise — popup titles should be one line wherever possible.
